clue.text: Clean finish

blocks.note: first meaning: to rub something until it shines
second meaning: refinement, the final smooth coat on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one instruction to tidy up and be done; each is a separate sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rubbing a surface bright and a noun for a refined final coat or elegance.

clue.text: Fuss when Dad meets former Australian tennis star

blocks.note: an informal word for father
Rod Laver, the Australian who won the Grand Slam twice in the 1960s

explanation.surface: A father gets flustered on being introduced to a tennis legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a lengthy, tiresome business or commotion, so it is a synonym for a fuss.

clue.text: Swing a bell! That's the ticket!

indicators.note: to swing is to move back and forth, so the following letters are set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone rings a bell in triumph on finding the perfect solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the ticket!' reads as a cheer, but 'ticket' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket in the sense of a tag or tab attached to goods showing price or details is a synonym for a label.

clue.text: Stood across street with artist, theologian and Liberal editor

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for street
Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
Doctor of Divinity
abbreviation for Liberal
standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A crowd of notables, painter, cleric, politician and journalist, stands lined up across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A string of crossword abbreviations: RA is a Royal Academician and DD a Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to stand with legs either side of something, spanning it, so the past tense matches having stood across it.

clue.text: To hear a chesty cough gives listener pain

indicators.note: the words before it yield up the letters they hold, so the solution sits inside that run of text

blocks.note: the letters run across the word break inside this phrase
surface padding that completes the picture of an illness

explanation.surface: Hearing someone hack away with a chest cough is unpleasant for the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough' is surface padding; the letters sit across 'hear a chesty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The listener here is the ear, the organ of hearing, so pain in it is an ache in the ear.

clue.text: Headless chicken with most chance to improve

indicators.note: without a head means the word loses its first letter
most of a word, not all of it, so one letter is dropped from it

blocks.note: a chicken is a hen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A panicking, headless chicken somehow has the best odds of getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless chicken' suggests panic; here it is a hen with its first letter cut, and 'most' trims the first letter of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise its quality or value, which is a straightforward synonym for making it better.

clue.text: Knight going back to Kentucky? It's dangerous!

indicators.note: going back means the title for a knight is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the title given to a knight
KY is the US postal abbreviation for Kentucky; 'to' places it next

explanation.surface: A knight is heading back to Kentucky, and the journey is hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky involves the possibility of harm or loss, so it is a synonym for hazardous or perilous.

clue.text: Record of events regarding rich clone mutation

indicators.note: a mutation is a change in genetic make-up, so the letters before it change their order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A report about a wealthy person's cloned double developing a genetic mutation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clone' and 'mutation' paint a genetics lab, which hides the anagram signal in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a factual written account of happenings in the order they occurred, a history.

clue.text: Returning, encounters note of respect

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the following words are read from right to left

blocks.note: encounters means meets
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: On coming back, someone meets a message expressing their regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration felt for someone, so it is a close synonym for respect.

clue.text: Entire performance follows short interval

indicators.note: short means the word is cut down, here to its usual abbreviated form
the performance word comes after the other piece, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: taken as written before cutting
an act is a performance or turn on stage

explanation.surface: A complete show comes after a brief intermission in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: INT is the standard abbreviation for interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, with nothing missing, so it is a synonym for complete or whole.

clue.text: Trainee sailor takes year in the never-ending maze

indicators.note: never-ending means the word has no end, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
able-bodied seaman
standard abbreviation for year
taken as written
taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A young recruit at sea spends a year lost in an endless maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' seems to describe the maze, but it cuts the last letter from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is a complicated network of winding paths, a classic synonym for a puzzle of passages.

clue.text: Fish spring traps

indicators.note: traps that spring snap open and shut, scattering their parts, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to an angler: set off the traps to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a season or a noun; here it is a verb telling the letters to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family, an example of the category.

clue.text: Virginia hat is acceptable

blocks.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A judgement that a hat from Virginia passes muster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valid is legitimate and sound, meeting the required standard, so it can be accepted.

clue.text: Anyone can be upset by aggravation

indicators.note: to be upset is to be knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A truism: anybody can be made cross by provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal and the definition both look like part of the same everyday remark about irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggravation in everyday use means irritation or exasperation, which is what an annoyance causes or is.

clue.text: Most of river bend allowed to become a stream

indicators.note: most of a word means only part of it is kept, so its final letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written before cutting
a U-bend or U-turn is a sharp curve shaped like the letter
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A river bend is permitted to shrink into a mere brook.
explanation.walkthrough: RIV is also a recognised abbreviation for river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a very small stream or brook, so the two describe the same kind of watercourse.

clue.text: Waver when sick in desert

indicators.note: in places the word for unwell inside the word for abandoning

blocks.note: sick means ill
to desert a place is to vacate it

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates on falling ill in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as a sandy noun; it is the verb to leave a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to keep changing one's mind and be indecisive, which is to waver.

clue.text: Bring about result

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to cause something to happen
second meaning: a noun, the outcome of a cause

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction, to produce a result, but the verb and the noun are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to cause or achieve a change; as a noun it means a consequence or outcome.

clue.text: Dreamer of disaster is prepared

indicators.note: a disaster throws everything into ruin and chaos, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who dreams of catastrophe is ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'forewarned is forearmed': knowing in advance lets you get ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forearmed means having equipped oneself in advance against trouble, so it means ready or prepared.

clue.text: Sharp detectives infiltrate returning US spies

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside an organisation, so one group goes inside the other
returning means going back, so the agency's initials are read backwards

blocks.note: Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
the Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: British detectives penetrate a group of American agents coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: The detectives sit inside the reversed spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sour or tart in taste, and figuratively cutting in tone, so it is a synonym for sharp.

clue.text: Windy city was stylish before

indicators.note: before tells the solver the past-time word comes after the other piece in order

blocks.note: chic means stylish
with 'before', means some time in the past
was before means in the past, ago

explanation.surface: A city that once had style, now just blustery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy City' is the well-known nickname of the US city in Illinois, so the definition is a proper noun in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illinois metropolis on Lake Michigan is famously nicknamed the Windy City.

clue.text: Asian bees buzz about rum cocktail

indicators.note: bees that buzz about fly here and there, so their letters move around
a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed in too

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Insects in Asia hover around someone's rum drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Burmese describes a person or thing from Burma, now Myanmar, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Scholars in charge point to fundamentals

blocks.note: Bachelors of Arts, graduates
standard abbreviation for in charge
south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Learned people in authority direct attention to the essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, a common crossword source of N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics are the essential elementary principles of a subject, the groundwork everything else rests on.

clue.text: Scramble to put into burial vault

blocks.note: the prefix en- means to put into, as in encase or entomb
a crypt is an underground burial chamber

explanation.surface: A rush to bury someone in a tomb beneath a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' looks like a hurried rush, but it is the definition in its coding sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a message is to jumble it so outsiders cannot read it, which is to put it into code.

clue.text: Distorted images cause wrinkly discrimination

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of its true shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Warped pictures of older people lead to prejudice against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrinkly' is British slang for an old person, so the definition means prejudice against the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice or unfair treatment on grounds of a person's years, typically against older people.

clue.text: Buildings with pictures of Queen in kitchens

indicators.note: in sets the royal abbreviation inside the word for ships' cooking rooms

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
galleys are ships' kitchens; this clue needs the rare spelling gallies

explanation.surface: Art museums display portraits of the monarch hung in the kitchens.
explanation.walkthrough: The standard plural is galleys, so the clue relies on a loose spelling for the kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleries are rooms or buildings where paintings and other artworks are put on public display.

clue.text: Built straight up

definitions.note: erect is a verb meaning to build; 'Built' is its past form

blocks.note: first meaning: constructed, as a building is put up
second meaning: upright, vertical

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a tall, vertical building, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to construct a building; as an adjective it means standing vertical or upright.

clue.text: Jelly snake I chew initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
taken as written
the first letter of chew

explanation.surface: A diner confesses to chomping on a snake set in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury clear jelly made from meat stock, used to set meats or eggs.

clue.text: Report a bit of a truce

indicators.note: a report is something spoken or heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a bit of something is a piece of it

explanation.surface: A news report containing a fragment of a ceasefire agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting, bringing a state of calm and an end to hostilities.

clue.text: Lunatic losing son becomes just silly

indicators.note: losing means a letter goes missing from the word before it

blocks.note: lunatic means mad, insane
standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A madman who loses his boy turns merely foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunatic' looks like a noun for a person; it is the adjective mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means lacking sense or significance, so it is a synonym for foolish or senseless.

clue.text: Go with Bill and guests

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
having company means having guests round

explanation.surface: An invitation to come along with Bill and the visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to travel or be together with them as an escort or companion.

clue.text: This car is a great performer

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1980s British family hatchback made by Austin Rover
second meaning: a distinguished musician or conductor

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a motoring advert praising a car's performance; the Austin model was a popular British car of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a British hatchback model and an eminent musician, especially a famous conductor.

clue.text: Most strange poem about daughter and saint

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the poem goes around the family member

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem
standard abbreviation for daughter
standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A very peculiar verse written about a girl and a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of odd, meaning the most peculiar or unusual of all.
